messages.subject: when FMI == NA
parts:
Yves,

In the parameterEstimates() function, you calculate fraction missing information using Savalei & Rhemtulla's (2012) method.  After step 2 (fitting the target model to the model-implied moments from step 1), you run a check to see whether any SEs == 0, then set those to NA before calculating FMI:

        SE.step2 <- ifelse(step2@Fit@se == 0, as.numeric(NA),
            step2@Fit@se)
        LIST$fmi <- 1 - (SE.step2^2/SE.orig^2)

I was wondering why you did this.  When would SE == 0?  If it is only approximately zero and rounds to zero even using double precision, isn't it justifiable to consider the FMI to be approximately 1 in this case?  I wouldn't expect such small SE when using truly complete data, and I don't necessarily disagree with setting it to missing in this function.  But I am running a simulation study, and I am wondering whether I should recode those NAs to 1s for my results, and my decision kind of rests on whether there is a reason you noticed that causes SEs to be 0 in step 2.

Thanks,

Terry

OK, that makes sense.  I checked my simulation results more closely, using parameter estimates to recreate the model-implied Mu and Sigma, and when I fit the model to them, I ended up seeing positive SEs (and chi-sq = 0) as expected.  So I'm not sure what went wrong in the replications where I saw FMI == NA, but I'm guessing it was a version issue with either lavaan or simsem.  The computing cluster I used was running R 2.15.2 and lavaan 0.5-12, but it's being updated now, and I'm guessing those replications won't be a problem if I run it again with the latest software.

Thanks, and Happy New Year!

Terry
